statement: Fix σ0 ∈ (1/2, 1) and suppose ∆0 = β∗ − σ0 > 0. Let C(s) = s + c, where c ∈ R is fixed. Suppose that numbers ω, σ satisfying 0 < ω < ∆0, σ > 0 can be chosen independently of the target character. For every primitive finite-order Hecke char- acter η, suppose there exist a finite set S, a holomorphic function Hη on ℜs > σ0, and a function Jη(Z) defined for all sufficiently large real Z, such that sup ℜs>σ0 |Hη(s) − 1| ≤ 1 2 . (2.2) For Z > 0, define fη(Z) = 1 2πi Z ℜs=2 ZC(s) e(s−5/6)2 Hη(s) LS F (s, η) ds. (2.3) Assume that, as Z → ∞, |Jη(Z)| ≪η ZC(σ0)+ω , (2.4) |Jη(Z) − fη(Z)| ≪η ZC(β∗)−σ . (2.5) The implied constants, lower thresholds, excluded set, and function Hη may depend on η. Then these assumptions contradict β∗ > σ0.
